links.reason: The friend's line 3 asks the queen to 'நிறையினைச் சிறைசெய்க', to keep restraint confined; nothing says the queen has already broken it, only that her heart sinks (உள்ளம் அளரும்). 'Too late' is read into the verse, and 1251 is about desire breaking the door, not a plea to keep it shut.

Verse 898 only says the host rings the banner-hall and the other kings make for the forest edge; it says nothing of allies or of the army as a limb of kingship. Kural 381's list of six (படை, குடி, கூழ், அமைச்சு, நட்பு, அரண்) is paired with a camp description on shared topic alone.

Kattiyangaran's கொல்வல்... என்று அல்லன நினைத்தல் செல்லார் gives the outcome to deeds (வினை), a real kin of 'ஊழிற் பெருவலி'. But the note's gain that the speech 'quotes a sanctioned teaching' is not true of the words: no run of the couplet appears, and வினை is not ஊழ் with the device-forestalling logic of 380.

Verse 42 gives the dream (இமில் ஏறு, இளங்கதிர்) and 44 reads it (சிறுவன் வந்துதிக்கும், நற்றவம் தாங்கி, வினை அறுத்து வீடு அடையும்); the later unit fulfils the earlier and the note says which. The pair shows prophecy fixing both lives before birth.

615 makes காமம் the கள் offered by the women's eyes, a poetic conceit; the Kural's three vices (பெண்டிர், கள், கவறு) as the company of the Fortune-forsaken are not echoed (no dice, no loss of fortune). The 'verdict' the couplet supposedly gives is not what the verse needs, and 'folds two of three vices' is thin.

Verse 260 does say the king is killed by கூற்றம், the woman, தான் செய்த பிழைப்பு, wealth and grace, which matches Ilango's 55 'அரைசியல் பிழைத்தோர்க்கு அறம் கூற்று ஆவது'. But the Cintamani king's fault is lust and misplaced trust, and the speaker is ironic, so 'neglect' and 'erring in kingship includes it' is an inference the verses do not state.

Both are wedding or festival decoration but only the SP unit has a jewelled canopy (வயிரமணித் தூண், நித்திலப் பந்தர்); 852 has gold plantains, emerald areca and full pots. A generic decorated hall is not a distinctive shared image, and the 'wishing-tree' the gains cites is not in the verse.

The speaker in 1179 says நீதி here is statecraft (scheming over fighting) and is reported by an unnamed warrior; Kural 546 says victory comes from the unbent sceptre. They answer different questions (how to win a war versus what makes a king win), so there is no incompatible claim, and the note's 'king's justice' mistakes நீதி for செங்கோல்.

2129 says Tirumal lifts a straight sceptre (செங்கோல்) with gods guarding (தேவர் காப்ப); it does not make the gods' guard depend on the sceptre. Kural 547 says justice guards the king, a real nearby idea, but the pair only juxtaposes two guards.

Both are pirithal poems where the man gives up the journey; but Akananuru 5 turns on the wife's silent look and the child's garland, and Kalittokai 17 on the friend's words 'மருந்து போல்'. 'A shared ending each voice claims' is only the common situation, not a qualification of either.

In 9 the king 'சொல்லாறு கேளான்' and is beaten by plot; in 1925 Civakan's line 2 holds strategy useless against a jackal, a claim the poem refutes in the next verses. The echo of contempt for counsel is real, but one is the narrator's account of a fall and the other a refuted boast, so the 'tension' and 'repeats his father's contempt' overstate.

Verse 2122 hails the வேலோன், இயக்கன், வென்றோன், வீரன்; Kama is not named, and the Yaksha is not Kama. The note and teaches say the crowd hails him as both Murugan and Kama, which the Tamil does not say; 1948 asks whether he is Murugan or Kama but 2122 answers only half.

906 is about men who fear their wives (அஞ்சுபவர்) and 1103 about the lover's delight in the beloved's arms; fear and love of a wife's shoulders are different attitudes to different things, not incompatible claims about one thing. Only the word தோள் and the heaven comparison are shared.

Vijayai's list (பகைவர் உள்ளம், பாம்பின் படர்ச்சி, மங்கையர் நெஞ்சம், மின்) says women's hearts do not run straight, and NaL 375's eel simile does say double conduct (மலங்கன்ன செய்கை). But the quatrain does not say the women 'sell intimacy' or form a class, and no dependence of one on the other is shown, so the 'widening from a trade to a sex' and the gains are read in.

1642 has the queens claim fragile hands, feet and waists from pollen, petal dust and a garland; Kural 1115 has the man joke that an anicham-wearer's waist will snap. Both use delicacy, but the Kural's stems and drum joke are not in the verse, and 'frailty as performance' is the marker's reading, not something the Kural gains.

1578 says வினை takes no account of the great in thought or those who have swum through learning (நீந்தினார் கலைகள்), and 373 says one's own understanding prevails over subtle books. These are close in topic, but 373's தன் உண்மை அறிவு prevailing is not the same as deed blinding understanding, so equating them as 'karma' is a reading, and line 2 is damaged.

The matrons pluck their hair and 'துறத்தல் மேயினார்' pondering the Lord's book; Kural 280 says shaving and long hair are needless if one gives up what the world condemns. 280 does not 'doubt' the shorn head, it dismisses outward marks, so 'the answer to the Kural's doubt' misstates the couplet, and the verse does not say hair-plucking comes with giving up the condemned.

2289 has a warrior who throws only at young elephants spend his spear on a man; Kural 772 ranks a spear that missed an elephant above an arrow that hit a hare. The elephant-only habit is a loose echo of the couplet's scale, but whether the spear missed, and the 'courtesy' reading, are not in either text.

Verse 1436 defines ஞானம், காட்சி, ஒழுக்கம் and says only when all three are full do both deeds pass (இருவினை கழியும்); Kural 357 says that one who knows உள்ளது needs no more thought of birth. The contrast of a single cause with a threefold one is real. It is weak because 357 does not say that knowing alone suffices and the couplet's verb is உணரான் in the text, read as உணரின் by the commentators.

1870 is a plain festival description (தோரணம், முரசு, வளைகள்) with no judgment on it; Kural 34's ஆகுல is noise as the mark of outward virtue. The pairing imports a standard the verse does not apply, and 'the poet does not apply it' means the verse gains nothing.

380 says the attendants read the king's sign (குறிப்பறிந்து) and withdraw, which does match Kural 701's கூறாமை நோக்கிக் குறிப்பறிவான். But this is an instance of the skill the couplet praises, not a qualification, and the verse is flagged uncertain.

1052 shows the nurse saying the match comes of old penance (தொல்வினைப் பயத்தின்) and telling the mother, who tells the father, which is the akam disclosure chain Kurinjippattu 1-22 argues for (அறத்தொடு நிற்றல்). The pair is a real convention match, but the epic does not extend the poem ('develops'), and the gain that the wedding follows is not in 1052.

934 simply shows the king riding his elephant under the white umbrella as splendour; NaL 21 says elephant-borne umbrella kings were all spoken of as dead. The same image of pomp, but nothing in 934 hints at its end, so reading the display as a reminder of mortality is supplied by the pairing.

575 has the king read the errand's end from Marusi's face (முகத்தினால் பொருள் முடிவு), a close case of 706's முகம் கடுத்தது காட்டும். It is an illustration; 'extends the couplet from a feeling to news' and the missing-case gain are thin.

983 makes நாண் a curtain (எழினி) hiding the prince in her heart; 155 makes her நாண் and grace droop a vine. Different women in different chapters and different uses of the common word நாண், so 'modesty shifts from ornament to screen' invents a development.

1792 shows the women's eyes leaving the kings for the prince; 1793 the king calls the maiden in. Nothing in 1793 answers or reverses 1792, they are two beats in story order, and 'the room has already leaned' is the marker's inference.

2873 tells the prince to drop wealth-greed bound with lies, deceit and dice (பொய், கைதவம், தாடல்), which touches Kural 283's ill-gained wealth that perishes. But 2873 gives no 'reason from this life, the loss of the gain': it calls these the dust of deeds, and the Kural's lost gain is not in the verse.

In 66 the friend calls the konrai foolish for taking the rain for the season, and 382 says the rain is untimely, but 66 too says the man's promised season has not come (வாரா அளவை), so both deny the season on the man's word. The claimed shift from blaming the tree to testing the season is not real.

241 ends a chapter with the king enjoying his wives and receiving tribute; it is not the epic's close, so 'the minor epic's close is not the great epic's close' is untrue of this unit. Civakan's renunciation (27) at the height of rule is a different matter; the contrast is a stated one, not a link.

173 has Tharusakan give his sister Padumai to Udayanan after a victory, and 114 has Harivara give Gunavati to Naga Kumara after he defeats the besieger. The shared plot motif is real, but two instances in different books show a pattern, not a distinctive image, and 'convention of the Jain kavyas' rests on two verses.

NaL 11 says the wise renounced in infancy foreseeing grey age; Purananuru 191 credits a good household and town for the poet's lack of grey hair. These are not incompatible claims about one thing, and the note's own condition ('on the reading that both speak of how to meet old age') shows the stretch.

2482 is a lovers' jest with the ornaments' complaint to a 'cruel-sceptred' king (கொடுங்கோலினன் ஆய்ந்து கேட்டு மருளான்); Kural 553 says a king who does not daily examine and do justice loses his land. A shared sceptre-and-hearing image, but no claim of the verse conflicts with the couplet, and the poet is not shown borrowing it.

Teaches cites 'the queen's chastity unfailing (வீடாத கற்பு)', which is not in verse 9; verse 9 says only that the king's desire grew thick (காமம் கனைந்து கன்றி) and he heard no counsel, not that it was desire for his wife, and the queen's flight is told separately (தேவி போகிச்). So the 'desire fixed on the wife' reading of 901 is not shown in the unit.

30 carries out the king's order of 22 (ஏவல் தனை நினைந்து... வவ்வி), which fulfils it. But the officer's seeing the pair's gentleness is in verse 29, not here, and 22's 'இயல்பினர்' is the king's description, so 'duty over mercy' is not what these two verses show.

Both units name Bharata: 1804 measures this king as the one after Bharata (பரதன்பின்), and 397 has the First Lord's grace make Bharata sole king. The Tamil fixes the same Bharata, and the pair shows the herald's yardstick is a grace-given sovereign.

215 gives past destiny (முனம் ஆகிய பான்மை) and the heart's way (மனமாம் நெறி) as the king's cause for running to the flower-haired woman; Kural 901 is about men who desire their wives. The verse does not say she is his wife, and 901 is not about rulers, so 'recognised fault of rulers' is added.

2302's rewards for those who die for the leader who raised them (தற்புறந் தந்து வைத்த) are near Kural 780's death that fills the sustainers' eyes with tears. But the 'bad master' point is from the story outside the verse, and the verse does not show the blind spot the gains names.

1255's laugh is a king at the report that his own army is broken (the verse is flagged uncertain), while Kural 774's laugh is a fighter's at his wound; only நகு is shared. The teaches also contradicts the note (a boast 'over others' loss' versus his own army's rout).

2691 makes spring's dance rest on the loosened bangles of forsaken women; the SP venbas make the cuckoo proclaim 'ஊடினீர் கூடுமின்' and ask what will become of the woman's heart. Both link spring and parted lovers, but 'the season's joy not shared by all' is generic, and SP also shows the cost.

133 has the king ask the sage and 134 gives his assurance; this is question and answer in story order. 'The answer to Yugi's lure is a prophecy that makes him wait' is not stated: in 134 he garlands Virisikai at once.

2014 calls knowledge from the texts a lamp (விளக்கு) and 2018 calls vision a lamp; both clear darkness, but 2018's darkness is karma and the two are not said to be stages of one light. A neighbouring sermon repeating a metaphor, with the staging supplied by the marker.

166 has the disguised pair pose as merchants (வாணிக உருவினோடு) in the enemy camp, which matches Kural 585's unsuspected form (கடாஅ உருவு). But they are infiltrating, not an ஒற்று by office, and the 'rule' and 'case' gains are thin.

2073's நாண் (bee of shame) driven off and கற்பு garland waved is a figure for disclosing to the friend (அறத்தினோடு நின்றாள்); 1251 says desire breaks நிறை bolted by நாண். Different words (கற்பு not நிறை) and no incompatible claim, so the 'tension' and 'ranking' are imposed.
